title: Communication 2
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. b1_communication (36) owns the speech-act verbs and the plain nouns — confirm, admit, deny, claim, insist, persuade, encourage, warn, remind, apologise, praise, criticise, statement, announcement, apology, complaint, compliment, rumour, gossip, silence, misunderstanding, phrase, quote, accent, tone, fluent, native, bilingual, slang, vocabulary, gesture, whisper, repeat, spell, translate — and b1_opinions owns the discourse chunks. Those carry this unit's sentences. The CORRECTED sweep caught two more the shipped pool cannot see: articulate and fluency, taught earlier today by leaf_personality_b2 and b2_suffixes_1, whose nodes are still `coming` (third unit running where this has happened — see the DECISIONS entry on pool blindness). Both dropped. What is left is the layer above naming the act: saying it well or badly (convey, clarify, elaborate, summarise, concise, vague, ambiguous, eloquent, blunt), what is meant but not said (imply, infer, literal, figurative, idiom, jargon, euphemism, sarcasm, irony) — which is where a fluent-sounding B2 speaker actually fails — and how people really talk (small talk, body language, eye contact, nod, shrug, interrupt, mumble, dialect, interpreter). C57 card 0 recaps Communication 1. C49 all 36 across three boards of 12. Build-the-family: clarify -> clarification, imply -> implication, ambiguous -> ambiguity, interpret -> interpreter, irony -> ironic; five derived forms, all bank items. A12 sense on blunt (direct) — the knife reading is the commoner one. E10 Use is rewrite production; every underline reconstructs its answer.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Communication 1 gave you the acts — confirm, admit, deny, claim, persuade, encourage, warn, apologise, praise, criticise — and the plain nouns: statement, apology, complaint, rumour, silence, misunderstanding, accent, tone, slang, gesture. Those words carry the sentences here. What is new is harder and later: saying a thing well or badly, and everything people mean without saying it.
cards.note_cz: Communication 1 ti dal řečové akty — confirm, admit, deny, claim, persuade, encourage, warn, apologise, praise, criticise — a jednoduchá podstatná jména: statement, apology, complaint, rumour, silence, misunderstanding, accent, tone, slang, gesture. Ta slova nesou zdejší věty. Nové je těžší a přijde později: říct věc dobře nebo špatně a všechno, co lidé myslí, aniž to řeknou.

blocks.title: Communication · saying it well or badly

sentences.en: A gesture can convey more than a sentence.
sentences.cz: Gesto může předat víc než věta.
accepts: A gesture can convey more than a sentence

sentences.en: Could you clarify what you meant before?
sentences.cz: Mohl bys upřesnit, co jsi tím myslel předtím?
accepts: Could you clarify what you meant before

sentences.en: She asked for clarification of that point.
sentences.cz: Požádala o upřesnění toho bodu.
accepts: She asked for clarification of that point

sentences.en: He refused to elaborate on his answer.
sentences.cz: Odmítl svou odpověď rozvést.
accepts: He refused to elaborate on his answer

sentences.en: Try to summarise the report in three lines.
sentences.cz: Zkus tu zprávu shrnout do tří řádků.
accepts: Try to summarise the report in three lines

sentences.en: It is easier to paraphrase than to translate.
sentences.cz: Přeformulovat je snazší než přeložit.
accepts: It is easier to paraphrase than to translate

sentences.en: His answer was concise and very clear.
sentences.cz: Jeho odpověď byla stručná a velmi jasná.
accepts: His answer was concise and very clear

sentences.en: The statement was vague and helped nobody.
sentences.cz: To prohlášení bylo vágní a nikomu nepomohlo.
accepts: The statement was vague and helped nobody

sentences.en: That phrase is ambiguous in both languages.
sentences.cz: Ta fráze je dvojznačná v obou jazycích.
accepts: That phrase is ambiguous in both languages

sentences.en: The ambiguity caused a real misunderstanding.
sentences.cz: Ta dvojznačnost způsobila skutečné nedorozumění.
accepts: The ambiguity caused a real misunderstanding

sentences.en: She is an eloquent speaker in two languages.
sentences.cz: Je výmluvná řečnice ve dvou jazycích.
accepts: She is an eloquent speaker in two languages

sentences.en: He gave a blunt but completely honest answer.
sentences.cz: Dal drsnou, ale naprosto upřímnou odpověď.
accepts: He gave a blunt but completely honest answer

sentences.en: Your tone seemed to imply something else.
sentences.cz: Zdálo se, že tvůj tón naznačuje něco jiného.
accepts: Your tone seemed to imply something else

sentences.en: Nobody liked the implication of that question.
sentences.cz: Nikomu se nelíbil náznak v té otázce.
accepts: Nobody liked the implication of that question

sentences.en: His silence lets us infer his real opinion.
sentences.cz: Jeho mlčení nám dává vyvodit jeho skutečný názor.
accepts: His silence lets us infer his real opinion

sentences.en: The literal meaning is not the useful one.
sentences.cz: Doslovný význam není ten užitečný.
accepts: The literal meaning is not the useful one

sentences.en: In the figurative sense it means something else.
sentences.cz: V přeneseném smyslu to znamená něco jiného.
accepts: In the figurative sense it means something else

sentences.en: Every idiom has to be learned as a whole.
sentences.cz: Každý idiom se musí naučit jako celek.
accepts: Every idiom has to be learned as a whole

sentences.en: The report was full of legal jargon.
sentences.cz: Ta zpráva byla plná právnického žargonu.
accepts: The report was full of legal jargon

sentences.en: People use a euphemism when the news is bad.
sentences.cz: Lidé použijí eufemismus, když jsou zprávy špatné.
accepts: People use a euphemism when the news is bad

sentences.en: Sarcasm does not travel well between languages.
sentences.cz: Sarkasmus mezi jazyky moc nefunguje.
accepts: Sarcasm does not travel well between languages

sentences.en: His sarcastic comment upset the whole team.
sentences.cz: Jeho sarkastická poznámka rozladila celý tým.
accepts: His sarcastic comment upset the whole team

sentences.en: The irony was lost on most of them.
sentences.cz: Ironii většina z nich nepochopila.
accepts: The irony was lost on most of them

sentences.en: It is ironic that he complained about noise.
sentences.cz: Je ironické, že si stěžoval na hluk.
accepts: It is ironic that he complained about noise

sentences.en: He is not good at small talk.
sentences.cz: Není moc dobrý ve zdvořilostní konverzaci.
accepts: He is not good at small talk

sentences.en: Her body language said more than her words.
sentences.cz: Její řeč těla říkala víc než slova.
accepts: Her body language said more than her words

sentences.en: In some cultures eye contact seems rude.
sentences.cz: V některých kulturách působí oční kontakt nezdvořile.
accepts: In some cultures eye contact seems rude

sentences.en: People nod when they want you to continue.
sentences.cz: Lidé přikývnou, když chtějí, abys pokračoval.
accepts: People nod when they want you to continue

sentences.en: A shrug can mean yes, no or nothing.
sentences.cz: Pokrčení ramen může znamenat ano, ne nebo nic.
accepts: A shrug can mean yes, no or nothing

sentences.en: Please do not interrupt while she is speaking.
sentences.cz: Prosím nepřerušuj ji, když mluví.
accepts: Please do not interrupt while she is speaking

sentences.en: He tends to mumble when he is nervous.
sentences.cz: Když je nervózní, mívá tendenci mumlat.
accepts: He tends to mumble when he is nervous

sentences.en: Her dialect is hard for other Czechs.
sentences.cz: Její nářečí je pro ostatní Čechy těžké.
accepts: Her dialect is hard for other Czechs

sentences.en: Somebody had to interpret for the visitors.
sentences.cz: Někdo musel návštěvníkům tlumočit.
accepts: Somebody had to interpret for the visitors

sentences.en: The interpreter worked for six hours.
sentences.cz: Ten tlumočník pracoval šest hodin.
accepts: The interpreter worked for six hours

sentences.en: His argument was quiet but very persuasive.
sentences.cz: Jeho argument byl tichý, ale velmi přesvědčivý.
accepts: His argument was quiet but very persuasive

sentences.en: The headline was misleading and later changed.
sentences.cz: Ten titulek byl zavádějící a později ho změnili.
accepts: The headline was misleading and later changed
